2. [ ] Verify the reported TNF-α endpoint, experimental conditions, and direction of effect in the study.
3. [ ] Record the evidence with provenance and provide a qualified yes/no conclusion.

Tool call: go_search_agent
Tool call input: {'knowledge_bases': ['pubmed_papers'], 'search_rounds_budget': 3, 'search_target': 'Search PubMed for controlled antibiotic perturbation studies in healthy human volunteers measuring ex vivo cytokine production or release by peripheral blood mononuclear cells, specifically TNF-alpha. Likely terms: gut microbiota, antibiotic treatment, mononuclear cells, healthy volunteers, lipopolysaccharide-stimulated TNF. Return exact paper citation/PMID and whether TNF release fell, rose, or was unchanged.'}

### Executed Code:
```python
import requests
terms=['(antibiotic OR antibiotics) AND gut microbiota AND (mononuclear OR PBMC OR "peripheral blood mononuclear") AND TNF','antibiotic-induced gut microbiota disruption healthy adults TNF-alpha mononuclear cells','antibiotic treatment healthy volunteers cytokine production mononuclear cells TNF']
for term in terms:
    u='https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi'
    p={'db':'pubmed','term':term,'retmode':'json','retmax':20}
    d=requests.get(u,params=p,timeout=30).json()
    ids=d['esearchresult']['idlist']
    print('\nQUERY',term,'\nIDS',ids)
    if ids:
        x=requests.get('https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi',params={'db':'pubmed','id':','.join(ids),'retmode':'json'},timeout=30).json()
        for i in ids:
            z=x['result'][i]
            print(i,z.get('title'),z.get('pubdate'))
```

```python
import requests, xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
pmid='27489950'
r=requests.get('https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi',params={'db':'pubmed','id':pmid,'retmode':'xml'},timeout=30)
root=ET.fromstring(r.text)
for tag in ['ArticleTitle','AbstractText','Journal','PubDate','AuthorList']:
    if tag=='AbstractText':
        vals=[(''.join(x.itertext()),x.attrib.get('Label','')) for x in root.findall('.//AbstractText')]
        print('ABSTRACT',vals)
    elif tag=='ArticleTitle': print('TITLE',''.join(root.find('.//ArticleTitle').itertext()))
    elif tag=='Journal': print('JOURNAL',root.findtext('.//Journal/Title'))
    elif tag=='PubDate': print('DATE',' '.join(root.find('.//PubDate').itertext()))
    elif tag=='AuthorList': print('AUTHORS',[a.findtext('LastName') for a in root.findall('.//Author')][:10])
print('DOI',root.findtext('.//ArticleId[@IdType="doi"]'))
```

Yes. The primary human study (Lankelma et al., 2016; PMID: 27489950) evaluated 12 healthy young men who received ciprofloxacin, vancomycin, and metronidazole for 7 days.

Key findings:

- Antibiotics significantly reduced gut microbial diversity.
- One day after treatment, isolated mononuclear cells produced less TNF-α after ex vivo lipopolysaccharide stimulation.
- The reduced TNF-α response returned to baseline six weeks after antibiotics were stopped.

This was a small proof-of-principle study, so it supports a reversible association rather than proving a permanent or universal effect.

FINAL DECISION: YES
